snippet.title: Flying a Drone with React and Node.js! (100% JavaScript!) — PART 1
snippet.description:
IBM Developer is giving away 2,000 DJI Tello drones and the tools needed to program it. I made this video to help them promote it. 

ENTER CONTEST: http://wes.io/663cf523e988
MORE DETAILS: http://wes.io/65b71fbd5728

CODEBASE: https://github.com/wesbos/javascript-drones


## Software Used
* React (with React Hooks!)
* Styled Components for styling
* Node.js and UDP4 sockets for communicating with drone
* Socket.io WebSockets for sending data to/from the browser
* Next.js for easy react setup
 ## Hardware Used

* DJI Tello Drone - http://wes.io/181e79ac97ee
*Extra Batteries - http://wes.io/4aa546e2af51- it comes with one and I bought two extra. For continual development I'd say you only need two — one in the charger and one in the drone. For flying away from your house you definitely need at least 3 as they only last about 10-15 mins.
* Fast Battery Charger with 4 slots - http://wes.io/bb90a237e2d5

snippet.title: Live Edit Sass with Takana and Sublime Text
snippet.description:
http://wesbos.com/live-edit-sass-takana/

A few days ago there was a buzz about a new Sublime Text package called [Takana](http://usetakana.com/) which claimed to do live editing of Sass. As someone who works on fairly large Sass projects, I was skeptical but decided to give it a short.

Wow, it is fast.

Takana is built upon the blazing fast C/C++ libsass and works in parity with Sublime Text to listen to any changes in your code (not just a save).

This is huge for those who work with Sass and Sublime Text in their workflow. Here is a video exploring how to install and get up and running with some HTML, Sass and the Bourbon library.
